kalshi.description: Win probability from Kalshi, a CFTC-regulated prediction market where real money is traded on event outcomes. Kalshi odds represent the consensus of market participants betting on game outcomes.
kalshi.methodology: The midpoint of the bid/ask spread for the 'Yes' contract on the game outcome market. Kalshi contracts settle at $1 if the event occurs and $0 otherwise, so the price directly represents the market's implied probability.

mlb.description: Official MLB win probability from the MLB Stats API. Computed from play-by-play data using run expectancy tables, leverage index, and game state (inning, outs, runners, score).
mlb.methodology: MLB's win probability model is based on historical play-by-play data across MLB seasons. It uses run expectancy matrices (based on base/out state), score differential, inning, home-field advantage, and updates on every pitch. Data sourced from the official MLB Stats API (statsapi.mlb.com).

stat_model.description: An open win probability model using sport-specific methodology. Clock sports (NFL, NBA, NHL) use a normal distribution model inspired by nflfastR. Baseball uses a Poisson run-scoring model based on Tom Tango's methodology.
stat_model.methodology: Clock sports: Based on Hal Stern's research. Final margin modeled as N(score_diff + spread × remaining_fraction, base_std × √remaining_fraction). Baseball: Based on Tom Tango's 'The Book'. Remaining runs modeled as Poisson(runs_per_half_inning × half_innings_remaining). Normal approximation gives P(home wins) accounting for asymmetric half-innings, walk-off rule, and home field advantage (~54% historical home win rate).

espn.description: ESPN's proprietary predictive model that updates on every play during live games. Uses game situation data including score, field position, down, distance, and time remaining.
espn.methodology: ESPN's internal win probability model, same data shown on ESPN.com game pages. Methodology is not publicly documented.
